messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@brightretail.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Annual commit question and onramp options

Hi Kimberly —

We’re finalizing our budget and want to lock an annual token commit for BrightRetail’s recommendation engine work. High-level ask: can you send a simple starter/growth/enterprise matrix with target token commits, per-token blended price, overage behavior, and any onboarding credits you’d consider for a 12-month agreement?

Two constraints on our side: 1) we need an initial 60-day pilot window with discounted evaluation usage (not fully billable), and 2) bookkeeping prefers monthly invoices with the ability to smooth billing across quarters.

Appreciate anything you can share this week — we’re aiming to get commercial terms to procurement by Apr 25.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Head of Data Products, BrightRetail
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Emma Li <emma@brightretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual commit question and onramp options

Emma — great to hear and thanks for the constraints. I put together a concise matrix and a couple of options that map to your evaluation and smoothing needs (attached). High level: Starter, Growth, Enterprise commits with explicit onramp credits and SLA anchors. Quick bullets below — attachment has the per-token decimals and ramp phasing.

- Starter (12mo): 150M tokens/year ~ $0.0065/token effective; 10% first-year carryover; 30% overage discount band after commit at $0.009/token. Includes one onboarding credit (equiv. $5k professional services).
- Growth (12mo): 750M tokens/year ~ $0.0052/token effective; 15% carryover; overage at $0.008/token; includes two onboarding credits + priority onboarding window (2 weeks).
- Enterprise (12mo): 3B tokens/year ~ $0.0040/token effective; 20% carryover; overage at $0.0065/token; SLA: 99.9% monthly availability or service credit; dedicated onboarding manager + 1 week POC support.

Pilot/onramp: We can model the 60-day pilot as a discounted bucket: up to 20% of Starter/Growth commit discounted at 50% for evaluation and credited back to your first invoice if you convert to a 12mo commit. Billing: monthly invoices with smoothing (we’ll invoice equal monthly installments against the committed spend and true-up usage).

Next steps: if this looks directionally right I’ll ask legal to prepare a short annex for the SLA and have procurement-ready terms (DocuSign link) and a simple billing schedule.

Attachments: BrightRetail_Commit_Matrix_v1.xlsx, SLA_Annex_Draft.pdf

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Can you confirm the effective per-token floors and whether the carryover % and overage brackets are acceptable? Also confirm whether we can commit an SLA credit at 99.9% for Enterprise (we typically offer 99.95 for Dedicated but 99.9 is okay for hosted with the enterprise package).

I flagged these points in the attached matrix: notable asks — 
• 50% discount on up to 20% of the pilot usage if they convert
• Monthly smoothing / equal installments with quarterly true-up

If you both OK this I’ll send a revised email to Emma with the commercial summary and DocuSign link.

Kim
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightRetail annual commit — onramp, credits & SLA anchors

Kim — quick thoughts from pricing: your numbers are close to our modeled LTV thresholds. A few suggested adjustments to keep margin:

- Starter: move effective to $0.0067/token (small lift) unless they take the onboarding credit as a billable PS add-on (we can keep $0.0065 if PS is extra).
- Growth: $0.00525/token, keep 15% carryover.
- Enterprise: hold at $0.0040/token but require a minimum quarterly commit (to avoid credit blowouts).

Pilot credit: acceptable at 50% up to 20% of committed usage if they sign a conversion clause within 45 days of pilot end.

SLA: 99.9% is fine but make sure legal's SLA annex includes the fallback routing policy and our maximum credit cap (cumulative credits in a 12mo period not to exceed 10% of committed spend).

—Karthik

One commercial play we should offer: 1 month of free premium support (concierge onboarding) for Growth and Enterprise if they commit before May 15 — frames urgency and keeps price intact. Also recommend a 5% extra discount on Enterprise if they accelerate to a 36-month prepay (optional).

I’ll drop a short note in HubSpot under the deal and add the legal ticket for the SLA appendix (see link).

Marissa

Emma — thanks again for the quick turnaround. We incorporated internal feedback and have a revised, procurement-ready summary below and attached DocuSign for the annex/term sheet. Key updates:

Summary offer (12-month, billed monthly with smoothing):
- Starter: 150M tokens/year — $0.0067/token effective; 10% carryover; overage at $0.009/token. Includes one $5k onboarding credit (or PS as billable).
- Growth: 750M tokens/year — $0.00525/token effective; 15% carryover; overage at $0.008/token. Includes two onboarding credits + 1 month complimentary concierge onboarding if signed before May 15.
- Enterprise: 3B tokens/year — $0.0040/token effective; 20% carryover; overage at $0.0065/token. SLA: 99.9% monthly availability with a capped service-credit mechanism (max cumulative credits = 10% committed spend/year). Option: additional 5% volumetric discount for 36-month prepaid terms. Minimum quarterly commit required.

Pilot/onramp: Up to 20% of the agreed commit can be used during a 60-day pilot at 50% discounted rate and will be credited toward the first invoice upon conversion if signed within 45 days of pilot completion.

Administrative items: we will smooth billing into equal monthly invoices with a quarterly true-up. Attached: BrightRetail_Commit_Matrix_v1.xlsx (breakpoints and blended math) and SLA_Annex_Draft.pdf. I’ve also created the DocuSign envelope for the term sheet: https://www.docusign.net/transactions/abc123.

If this looks good I can route to legal for an annex and to procurement (I included the HubSpot deal link in the header). Proposed commercial next step: sign the term sheet, schedule a 60-day pilot start on May 3, and agree a POC week of May 17 for integration validation.

Quick yes/no from you on the pilot start and the May 15 signing incentive and I’ll lock things in.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
